title: Powers of Natural Guardian — Section 8 HMGA

content.overview: Section 8 of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 regulates the powers of a natural guardian of a Hindu minor. The guardian may do all acts necessary or reasonable and proper for the benefit of the minor or the minor’s estate, but may not bind the minor by a personal covenant. Immovable property of the minor cannot be mortgaged, charged, transferred by sale, gift, exchange or otherwise, or leased for terms beyond the statutory limits, without prior permission of the court.
content.glance: Ask: (1) Natural guardian under s. 6? (2) Act for benefit of minor/estate? (3) Immovable dealing needing court permission? (4) Personal covenant barred?
content.study:
Section 8 balances management power with protective limits. Unauthorized transfers of immovable property are voidable at the instance of the minor or any person claiming under the minor.

Court permission is the safeguard for major alienations of immovable property.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: General power
sections.body: Acts necessary or reasonable and proper for the benefit of the minor or the minor’s estate.

sections.heading: No personal covenant
sections.body: Guardian cannot bind the minor by a personal covenant.

sections.heading: Immovable property limits
sections.body: Mortgage, charge, sale, gift, exchange or other transfer, and long leases, require prior court permission.

sections.heading: Voidable transfers
sections.body: Dealings in breach of the section are voidable at the instance of the minor or persons claiming under the minor.

sections.heading: Benefit standard
sections.body: Power is fiduciary; benefit of the minor is the touchstone.

examples.title: Sale without permission
examples.body: Natural guardian sells minor’s immovable property without court permission — transfer voidable at the minor’s instance.

hypotheticals.question: Can a natural guardian lease minor’s land for 10 years without permission?
hypotheticals.analysis: Long leases beyond the statutory limits require prior court permission under s. 8.

distinctions.title: s. 8 powers vs s. 6 status
distinctions.left: What the natural guardian may do.

misconceptions.trap: Natural guardian has unlimited power over the minor’s property.
misconceptions.correction: Immovable alienations and long leases need prior court permission; personal covenants cannot bind the minor.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the powers of a natural guardian under HMGA s. 8.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: General benefit power; no personal covenant; immovable limits and court permission; voidable dealings.
